claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells represent a small proportion of thymic iNKT cells.
source: We demonstrate here that the small proportion of thymic iNKT and mucosal associated invariant T cells that express CCR7 represent a multi-potent progenitor pool that gives rise to effector subsets within the thymus.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells represent a multi-potent progenitor pool that gives rise to effector subsets within the thymus.
source: We demonstrate here that the small proportion of thymic iNKT and mucosal associated invariant T cells that express CCR7 represent a multi-potent progenitor pool that gives rise to effector subsets within the thymus.
evidence: Main finding stated in abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells emigrate from the thymus in a Klf2 dependent manner.
source: Using intra-thymic labeling, we also showed that CCR7+ iNKT cells emigrate from the thymus in a Klf2 dependent manner, and undergo further maturation after reaching the periphery.
evidence: Stated in abstract and demonstrated through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments with Klf2-deficient cells.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells undergo further maturation after reaching the periphery.
source: Using intra-thymic labeling, we also showed that CCR7+ iNKT cells emigrate from the thymus in a Klf2 dependent manner, and undergo further maturation after reaching the periphery.
evidence: Demonstrated through tracking of recent thymic emigrants and analysis of maturation markers.

claim: Ccr7 deficiency impairs differentiation of iNKT effector subsets.
source: Ccr7 deficiency impaired differentiation of iNKT effector subsets and localization to the medulla.
evidence: Shown through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments comparing Ccr7 KO and WT cells.

claim: Ccr7 deficiency impairs localization of iNKT cells to the medulla.
source: Ccr7 deficiency impaired differentiation of iNKT effector subsets and localization to the medulla.
evidence: Demonstrated through immunofluorescence and histocytometry analysis of thymic sections.

claim: Thymic NKT1 cells are resident and not derived from the peripheral pool.
source: Parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer showed that thymic NKT1 and NKT17 were resident—they were not derived from and did not contribute to the peripheral pool.
evidence: Demonstrated through parabiosis experiments showing >95% of thymic iNKT cells were of host origin.

claim: Thymic NKT17 cells are resident and not derived from the peripheral pool.
source: Parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer showed that thymic NKT1 and NKT17 were resident—they were not derived from and did not contribute to the peripheral pool.
evidence: Demonstrated through parabiosis experiments showing >95% of thymic iNKT cells were of host origin.

claim: Thymic NKT1 cells do not contribute to the peripheral pool.
source: Parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer showed that thymic NKT1 and NKT17 were resident—they were not derived from and did not contribute to the peripheral pool.
evidence: Demonstrated through intra-thymic transfer experiments showing transferred Tbx21GFP+ NKT1 cells were rarely recovered from spleen.

claim: Thymic NKT17 cells do not contribute to the peripheral pool.
source: Parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer showed that thymic NKT1 and NKT17 were resident—they were not derived from and did not contribute to the peripheral pool.
evidence: Demonstrated through parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: Each thymic iNKT effector subset produces distinct factors that influence T cell development.
source: Finally, each thymic iNKT effector subset produces distinct factors that influence T cell development.
evidence: Demonstrated through analysis of IFN-γ production by NKT1 cells and RANKL production by NKT2 and NKT17 cells.

claim: iNKT cells are αβ T cells expressing semi-invariant T cell receptors (TCR) that respond to self-lipids or foreign-lipids presented by CD1d.
source: Invariant natural killer T (iNKT) cells are αβ T cells expressing semi-invariant T cell receptors (TCR) that respond to self-lipids or foreign-lipids presented by the MHC-I like antigen-presenting molecule CD1d (Bendelac et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bendelac et al., 2007.

claim: iNKT cells secrete a variety of cytokines early after stimulation or in the steady state to influence immune responses and tissue homeostasis.
source: They are numerically less abundant than conventional peptide recognizing CD4 and CD8 T cells but profoundly important, secreting a variety of cytokines early after stimulation or in the steady state to influence immune responses and tissue homeostasis (Lee et al., 2013; Lynch et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2015; Engel and Kronenberg, 2014).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: iNKT cells display substantial functional heterogeneity despite being monospecific.
source: Previous work has demonstrated that despite being monospecific, iNKT cells display substantial functional heterogeneity (Coquet et al., 2008; Doisne et al., 2009; Doisne et al., 2011; Havenar-Daughton et al., 2012; Michel et al., 2007; Terashima et al., 2008; Watarai et al., 2012), being composed of three predominant effector subsets, NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 according to the expression of key transcription factors and cytokine production (Lee et al., 2013; Gapin, 2016).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: iNKT cells are composed of three predominant effector subsets: NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17.
source: Previous work has demonstrated that despite being monospecific, iNKT cells display substantial functional heterogeneity (Coquet et al., 2008; Doisne et al., 2009; Doisne et al., 2011; Havenar-Daughton et al., 2012; Michel et al., 2007; Terashima et al., 2008; Watarai et al., 2012), being composed of three predominant effector subsets, NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 according to the expression of key transcription factors and cytokine production (Lee et al., 2013; Gapin, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013 and Gapin, 2016.

claim: NKT1 cells are T-bet+ PLZFlow and produce IFN-γ.
source: For instance, NKT1 cells are T-bet+ PLZFlow and produce IFN-γ; NKT17 cells are ROR-γt+ PLZFint and produce IL-17; while NKT2 cells are PLZFhigh, and produce IL-4 (Lee et al., 2013; Gapin, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013 and Gapin, 2016.

claim: NKT17 cells are ROR-γt+ PLZFint and produce IL-17.
source: For instance, NKT1 cells are T-bet+ PLZFlow and produce IFN-γ; NKT17 cells are ROR-γt+ PLZFint and produce IL-17; while NKT2 cells are PLZFhigh, and produce IL-4 (Lee et al., 2013; Gapin, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013 and Gapin, 2016.

claim: NKT2 cells are PLZFhigh and produce IL-4.
source: For instance, NKT1 cells are T-bet+ PLZFlow and produce IFN-γ; NKT17 cells are ROR-γt+ PLZFint and produce IL-17; while NKT2 cells are PLZFhigh, and produce IL-4 (Lee et al., 2013; Gapin, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013 and Gapin, 2016.

claim: iNKT cells are positively selected in the thymus in response to agonist interactions with self-lipid/CD1d expressing double positive thymocytes (DP) in the thymic cortex.
source: iNKT cells are positively selected in the thymus, in response to agonist interactions with self-lipid/CD1d expressing double positive thymocytes (DP) in the thymic cortex (Egawa et al., 2005; Gapin et al., 2001; Moran et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Egawa et al., 2005; Gapin et al., 2001; Moran et al., 2011.

claim: Stage 0 iNKT cells express a high level of CD24 and are considered the most immature.
source: At this point the cells express a high level of CD24, and are considered the most immature, or 'stage 0'.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Mature functionally competent effector iNKT cells localize predominantly in the thymic medulla.
source: In contrast, matured functionally competent effector iNKT cells localize predominantly in the thymic medulla (Lee et al., 2015), and thymic medullary epithelial cells impact their functional maturation (White et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2015 and White et al., 2014.

claim: Thymic medullary epithelial cells impact iNKT cell functional maturation.
source: In contrast, matured functionally competent effector iNKT cells localize predominantly in the thymic medulla (Lee et al., 2015), and thymic medullary epithelial cells impact their functional maturation (White et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to White et al., 2014.

claim: CD44 and NK1.1 markers are heterogeneously expressed on mature cytokine producing iNKT effector subsets.
source: However, more recent work showed that these markers are heterogeneously expressed on the mature cytokine producing iNKT effector subsets (Coquet et al., 2008; Doisne et al., 2009; Doisne et al., 2011; Havenar-Daughton et al., 2012; Michel et al., 2007; Terashima et al., 2008; Watarai et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: IL-4− PLZFhi iNKT cells retain precursor potential and can convert to T-bet+ NKT1 cells in the thymus.
source: However, IL-4− PLZFhi iNKT cells still retained precursor potential, and could convert to T-bet+ NKT1 cells in the thymus (Lee et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2013.

claim: There is heterogeneity within the PLZFhi iNKT cell population.
source: These results suggest there is heterogeneity within the PLZFhi iNKT cell population, and led us to hypothesize that there exists a population of progenitor cells within the PLZFhi iNKT cells.
evidence: Inference based on previous findings from Lee et al., 2013.

claim: IL-4− PLZFhi iNKT cells have low similarity with the three effector subsets according to transcriptional profiling by RNA-Seq.
source: Indeed, transcriptional profiling by RNA-Seq indicated IL-4− PLZFhi iNKT cells had low similarity with the three effector subsets, including IL-4 producing PLZFhi iNKT cells (Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2016.

claim: Single cell RNA-Seq analysis suggests there might be a progenitor population within the PLZFhi iNKT cells.
source: Single cell RNA-Seq analysis from another group also suggested there might be a progenitor population within the PLZFhi iNKT cells (Engel et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Engel et al., 2016.

claim: Most thymic iNKT cells are Rag2GFP negative.
source: We found most thymic iNKT cells were Rag2GFP negative, while a small proportion of iNKT cells express Rag2GFP (Figure 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A using Rag2GFP reporter mice.

claim: iNKT cells with the highest GFP also express CD24 and high level of CD69, indicating they are stage 0 iNKT cells.
source: The iNKT cells with the highest GFP also express CD24 and high level of CD69, indicating they are stage 0 iNKT cells that are immediate after agonist selection (Figure 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells express high to intermediate amounts of GFP, suggesting they are immature and recently derived from stage 0 iNKT cells.
source: CCR7+ iNKT cells expressed high to intermediate amounts of GFP, suggesting they are immature and recently derived from stage 0 iNKT cells (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A using Rag2GFP reporter mice.

claim: The Rag2GFP lowest cells (most mature) do not express CCR7.
source: Whereas, the Rag2GFP lowest cells (most mature) did not express CCR7 (Figure 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1A through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells are predominantly NK1.1– CD44lo (stage 1) but also include some NK1.1− CD44+ cells (stage 2).
source: According to the conventional 'staging' system of iNKT cells in B6 mice, CCR7+ iNKT cells were predominantly NK1.1– CD44lo (stage 1) but also included some NK1.1− CD44+ cells (stage 2) (Figure 1B), although most NK1.1− CD44+ (stage 2) cells were not CCR7+ as this gate mostly included functionally mature NKT2 and NKT17 cells, and NKT1 cells were NK1.1+ CD44+ (stage 3) (Figure 1B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1B through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Most CCR7+ iNKT cells do not express T-bet, ROR-γt, or IL-4 (human CD2).
source: Furthermore, most CCR7+ iNKT cells did not express T-bet, ROR-γt, IL-4 (human CD2) (Figure 1C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1C through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells express abundant PLZF and LEF1.
source: Rather, CCR7+ iNKT cells expressed abundant PLZF and LEF1 (Figure 1C), which are both essential for iNKT cells development and proliferation (Carr et al., 2015; Savage et al., 2008; Kovalovsky et al., 2008).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1C through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: PLZF and LEF1 are both essential for iNKT cell development and proliferation.
source: Rather, CCR7+ iNKT cells expressed abundant PLZF and LEF1 (Figure 1C), which are both essential for iNKT cells development and proliferation (Carr et al., 2015; Savage et al., 2008; Kovalovsky et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to Carr et al., 2015; Savage et al., 2008; Kovalovsky et al., 2008.

claim: Most CCR7+ iNKT cells express Ki67 (>75%) compared to the three effector subsets or the stage 0 iNKT cells.
source: Most CCR7+ iNKT cells expressed Ki67 (>75%) compared to the three effector subsets or the stage 0 iNKT cells (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C), suggesting they are highly proliferative.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells are highly proliferative.
source: Most CCR7+ iNKT cells expressed Ki67 (>75%) compared to the three effector subsets or the stage 0 iNKT cells (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B,C), suggesting they are highly proliferative.
evidence: Inferred from high Ki67 expression shown in Figure 1D.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells have much lower level of Nur77GFP than stage 0 iNKT cells.
source: We showed CCR7+ iNKT cells had much lower level of Nur77GFP than stage 0 iNKT cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D,E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D,E using Nur77GFP reporter mice.

claim: Egr2 is highly expressed in iNKT thymic precursors.
source: A previous study suggested that the transcription factor Egr2 controls the development of iNKT cells and is highly expressed in iNKT thymic precursors (Seiler et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Seiler et al., 2012.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells express high levels of Egr2.
source: Consistently, we observed a high expression of Egr2 in CCR7+ iNKT cells while most thymic iNKT cells were positive for Egr2 expression (Figure 1C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1C through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: iNKT cells go through the CD4+ stage after stage 0 iNKT cells.
source: Moreover, consistent with a previous report that iNKT cells go through the CD4+ stage after stage 0 iNKT cells (Benlagha et al., 2005), we showed CCR7+ iNKT cells indeed exclusively expressed CD4, but not CD8 (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by citation to Benlagha et al., 2005.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells exclusively express CD4, but not CD8.
source: Moreover, consistent with a previous report that iNKT cells go through the CD4+ stage after stage 0 iNKT cells (Benlagha et al., 2005), we showed CCR7+ iNKT cells indeed exclusively expressed CD4, but not CD8 (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Five days after intra-thymic transfer, CCR7+ iNKT cells differentiate into all three effector subsets: NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 cells.
source: Five days after intra-thymic transfer, all three effector subsets, NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 cells were detected (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1E,F through intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells differentiate into NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 cells in the spleen after intravenous injection.
source: To test the precursor potential of thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells in the periphery, we also injected the sorted CCR7+ thymocytes intravenously into congenic hosts and detected substantial differentiation of NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 cells in the spleen (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F,G), demonstrating that iNKT progenitors do not require the thymus for effector differentiation.
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F,G through intravenous injection experiments.

claim: iNKT progenitors do not require the thymus for effector differentiation.
source: To test the precursor potential of thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells in the periphery, we also injected the sorted CCR7+ thymocytes intravenously into congenic hosts and detected substantial differentiation of NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 cells in the spleen (Figure 1—figure supplement 2F,G), demonstrating that iNKT progenitors do not require the thymus for effector differentiation.
evidence: Demonstrated through intravenous injection experiments showing differentiation in spleen.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells are clearly separated from the three major effector subsets according to SPADE analysis.
source: Importantly, CCR7+ iNKT cells were clearly separated from the three major effector subsets, (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 2H).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1G and Figure 1—figure supplement 2H through SPADE analysis.

claim: Within PLZFhi iNKT cells, CCR7 and PD-1 best distinguish progenitors from effectors.
source: Within the PLZFhi iNKT cells, CCR7 and PD-1 best distinguished progenitors from effectors, and only PLZFhi PD-1+ iNKT cells produced IL-4 (human CD2+) in the steady state (Figure 1H).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1H through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Only PLZFhi PD-1+ iNKT cells produce IL-4 (human CD2+) in the steady state.
source: Within the PLZFhi iNKT cells, CCR7 and PD-1 best distinguished progenitors from effectors, and only PLZFhi PD-1+ iNKT cells produced IL-4 (human CD2+) in the steady state (Figure 1H).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1H through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ MAIT cells have high to intermediate Rag2GFP expression while being low for CD24 and CD69 expression.
source: Indeed, similar to CCR7+ iNKT cells (Figure 1A), CCR7+ MAIT cells also had high to intermediate Rag2GFP expression while being low for CD24 and CD69 expression, suggesting they are also at an early stage of development after agonist selection (Figure 1I).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1I through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ MAIT cells are at an early stage of development after agonist selection.
source: Indeed, similar to CCR7+ iNKT cells (Figure 1A), CCR7+ MAIT cells also had high to intermediate Rag2GFP expression while being low for CD24 and CD69 expression, suggesting they are also at an early stage of development after agonist selection (Figure 1I).
evidence: Inferred from Rag2GFP, CD24, and CD69 expression patterns shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Mature MAIT cells are composed of ROR-γt+ and T-bet+ MAIT cells.
source: Mature MAIT cells are composed of only two distinct effector subpopulations, ROR-γt+ and T-bet+ MAIT cells (Koay et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Koay et al., 2016.

claim: CCR7+ MAIT cells do not express T-bet or ROR-γt.
source: CCR7+ MAIT cells did not express T-bet or ROR-γt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7+ MAIT cells are progenitor populations that give rise to their corresponding MAIT effector cells.
source: Together, these data suggest that both CCR7+ iNKT cells and CCR7+ MAIT cells are progenitor populations that give rise to their corresponding iNKT and MAIT effector cells.
evidence: Inferred from the developmental characteristics and marker expression of CCR7+ MAIT cells.

claim: Recent thymic emigrant iNKT cells (RTE iNKT) can be detected using intra-thymic injection of NHS-biotin followed by magnetic enrichment.
source: Using this tool, recent thymic emigrant iNKT cells (called 'RTE iNKT') could be readily detected (Figure 2A), while biotin− iNKT cells within the unbound fraction are largely (>97%) 'old' iNKT cells—those cells already residing in the periphery before intra-thymic labeling (Figure 2A).
evidence: Demonstrated through intra-thymic biotin labeling experiments shown in Figure 2A.

claim: RTE iNKT cells have higher Rag2GFP compared to biotin− iNKT cells.
source: As expected, the RTE iNKT cells have higher Rag2GFP compared to biotin− iNKT cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: RTE iNKT cells are highly enriched for CCR7+ cells compared to thymic or biotin− iNKT cells.
source: We further found that RTE iNKT cells were highly enriched for CCR7+ cells compared to thymic or biotin− iNKT cells (Figure 2B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2B through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Within RTE iNKT cells, CCR7+ cells express higher Rag2GFP than CCR7– cells.
source: Moreover, within the RTE iNKT cells, the CCR7+ cells expressed higher Rag2GFP than CCR7– cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Rag2GFP+ splenic iNKT cells are predominantly CCR7+.
source: In agreement with these data, Rag2GFP+ splenic iNKT cells were predominantly CCR7+, while most Rag2GFP– splenic iNKT cells did not express CCR7 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Klf2 is crucial for the thymic egress of conventional CD4 and CD8 lymphocytes.
source: The transcription factor Kruppel-like factor 2 (Klf2) is crucial for the thymic egress of conventional CD4 and CD8 lymphocytes (Carlson et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Carlson et al., 2006.

claim: Klf2-deficient conventional CD4 and CD8 T cells are enriched in the thymus and underrepresented amongst peripheral cells.
source: As expected, Klf2-deficient conventional CD4 and CD8 T cells were enriched in the thymus and underrepresented amongst peripheral cells (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2C,D through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: Klf2-deficient iNKT cells are enriched in the thymus and underrepresented amongst RTE and biotin− iNKT cell populations.
source: Similarly, Klf2-deficient iNKT cells were also enriched in the thymus and underrepresented amongst RTE and biotin− iNKT cells populations (Figure 2C,D), suggesting thymic emigration of iNKT cells is dependent on Klf2.
evidence: Shown in Figure 2C,D through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: Thymic emigration of iNKT cells is dependent on Klf2.
source: Similarly, Klf2-deficient iNKT cells were also enriched in the thymus and underrepresented amongst RTE and biotin− iNKT cells populations (Figure 2C,D), suggesting thymic emigration of iNKT cells is dependent on Klf2.
evidence: Inferred from the enrichment of Klf2-deficient iNKT cells in thymus and their underrepresentation in periphery.

claim: Klf2 regulates expression of S1PR1.
source: As Klf2 regulates expression of S1PR1 (Carlson et al., 2006), this is consistent with the previously reported requirement for S1PR1 in iNKT cell thymic egress (Allende et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Carlson et al., 2006.

claim: S1PR1 is required for iNKT cell thymic egress.
source: As Klf2 regulates expression of S1PR1 (Carlson et al., 2006), this is consistent with the previously reported requirement for S1PR1 in iNKT cell thymic egress (Allende et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Allende et al., 2008.

claim: Thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells highly express Klf2 comparable to mature thymic CD8 single positive (SP) thymocytes.
source: The majority of thymic iNKT cells did not express Klf2, though thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells or RTE iNKT cells highly expressed Klf2 comparable to mature thymic CD8 single positive (SP) thymocytes or RTE CD8 T cells, respectively (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2E using Klf2GFP reporter mice.

claim: RTE iNKT cells highly express Klf2 comparable to RTE CD8 T cells.
source: The majority of thymic iNKT cells did not express Klf2, though thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells or RTE iNKT cells highly expressed Klf2 comparable to mature thymic CD8 single positive (SP) thymocytes or RTE CD8 T cells, respectively (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A using Klf2GFP reporter mice.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells are the predominant thymic emigrating iNKT cell.
source: Altogether, these results suggest that CCR7+ iNKT cells are the predominant thymic emigrating iNKT cell, and they do so in a Klf2 dependent manner.
evidence: Inferred from the enrichment of CCR7+ cells among RTE iNKT and their Klf2 expression.

claim: T-bet+ and ROR-γt+ cells are substantially underrepresented amongst RTE iNKT cells compared to total thymic iNKT cells.
source: In further characterizing RTE iNKT cells, we observed that T-bet+, and ROR-γt+ cells were substantially underrepresented amongst RTE iNKT cells compared to total thymic iNKT cells (Figure 3A,B), suggesting that both T-bet+ NKT1 and ROR-γt+ NKT17 cells may be resident in the thymus.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3A,B through flow cytometry analysis of RTE iNKT cells.

claim: T-bet+ NKT1 and ROR-γt+ NKT17 cells may be resident in the thymus.
source: In further characterizing RTE iNKT cells, we observed that T-bet+, and ROR-γt+ cells were substantially underrepresented amongst RTE iNKT cells compared to total thymic iNKT cells (Figure 3A,B), suggesting that both T-bet+ NKT1 and ROR-γt+ NKT17 cells may be resident in the thymus.
evidence: Inferred from their underrepresentation among RTE iNKT cells.

claim: Thymic NK1.1+ iNKT cells are retained long-term.
source: This is consistent with the previously reported long-term retention of thymic NK1.1+ iNKT cells (Berzins et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Berzins et al., 2006.

claim: Thymic NKT2 cells that produce high levels of IL-4 (human CD2) are less likely to be found amongst RTE.
source: Similarly, thymic NKT2 cells that produce high levels of IL-4 (human CD2) were also less likely to be found amongst RTE (Figure 3B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3B through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: RTE NKT1 cells fail to express Qa2, while thymic T-bet+ NKT1 and splenic biotin− T-bet+ NKT1 cells both express high level of Qa2.
source: However, cells within this small population failed to express Qa2, while the thymic T-bet+ NKT1 and splenic biotin− T-bet+ NKT1 cells both expressed high level of Qa2 (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C,D through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Qa2 is commonly used to mark the most mature thymocytes.
source: As Qa2 has commonly been used to mark the most mature thymocytes, this suggests that RTE NKT1 cells were recently derived from progenitors, as opposed to emigrating as a mature cell.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: RTE NKT1 cells were recently derived from progenitors, as opposed to emigrating as a mature cell.
source: As Qa2 has commonly been used to mark the most mature thymocytes, this suggests that RTE NKT1 cells were recently derived from progenitors, as opposed to emigrating as a mature cell.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of Qa2 expression in RTE NKT1 cells.

claim: There is a progressive increase in Qa2 in RTE NKT1 cells over 72 hr after intra-thymic labeling.
source: Indeed, in cells collected 72 hr after intra-thymic labeling, we observed a progressive increase in Qa2 in RTE NKT1 cells (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3C,D through flow cytometry analysis at different time points.

claim: RTE T-bet+ NKT1 express significantly higher PLZF at 24 hr, while the expression is down regulated over 72 hr.
source: Furthermore, RTE T-bet+ NKT1 expressed significantly higher PLZF at 24 hr, while the expression was down regulated over 72 hr (Figure 3D).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3D through flow cytometry analysis at different time points.

claim: RTE T-bet+ NKT1 cells were not directly derived from mature thymic NKT1 cells, but more likely recently differentiated from precursors.
source: Taken together, these results strongly suggested that RTE T-bet+ NKT1 cells were not directly derived from mature thymic NKT1 cells, but more likely recently differentiated from precursors.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of Qa2 expression and high PLZF expression in RTE NKT1 cells.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells rapidly emigrate to the periphery and serve as precursors that give rise to iNKT effector subsets.
source: To further support this hypothesis, we sorted CCR7+ thymocytes (CD4+ Tbx21GFP– huCD2– CD24– CD8–) from Tbx21GFP/KN2 mice and injected them intra-thymically into congenic hosts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A). Five days later, all three effector subsets, NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 cells were detected in the spleen (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C), indicating CCR7+ iNKT cells rapidly emigrate to the periphery and serve as precursors that give rise to iNKT effector subsets.
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B,C through intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: iNKT cells derived from Ccr7-deficient donors show substantially impaired differentiation of all three iNKT effector subsets.
source: As expected, the generation of double positive (DP) thymocytes was not affected by the absence of CCR7, while iNKT cells derived from the Ccr7-deficient donors showed substantially impaired differentiation of all three iNKT effector subsets (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4A,B through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: The generation of double positive (DP) thymocytes is not affected by the absence of CCR7.
source: As expected, the generation of double positive (DP) thymocytes was not affected by the absence of CCR7, while iNKT cells derived from the Ccr7-deficient donors showed substantially impaired differentiation of all three iNKT effector subsets (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4A,B through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: MAIT cell differentiation is severely impaired when lacking cell-intrinsic CCR7.
source: In mixed bone marrow chimeras with wild type and Ccr7-deficient bone marrow cells, MAIT cell differentiation was also severely impaired when lacking cell-intrinsic CCR7 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–C through mixed bone marrow chimera experiments.

claim: CCR7 responds to CCL21a produced in the thymic medulla and is essential for migration of thymocytes from the cortex to medulla.
source: It was recently shown that CCR7 responds to CCL21a produced in the thymic medulla and is essential for migration of thymocytes from the cortex to medulla (Kozai et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kozai et al., 2017.

claim: Ccr7-deficient iNKT cells show significantly reduced localization in the thymic medulla compared to wild type iNKT cells.
source: Moreover, Ccr7-deficient iNKT cells showed significantly reduced localization in the thymic medulla compared to wild type iNKT cells (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 4D–F through immunofluorescence and histocytometry analysis.

claim: CCR7 directs iNKT cells to localize in thymic medulla.
source: These data suggest that, CCR7 not only plays an indispensable role in differentiation of thymic iNKT effector subsets, but also directs iNKT cells to localize in thymic medulla.
evidence: Inferred from the reduced medullary localization of Ccr7-deficient iNKT cells.

claim: Splenic CD4 or CD8 T cells are present at 50:50 ratios in parabiotic pairs.
source: Splenic CD4 or CD8 T cells were present at 50:50 ratios in parabiotic pairs consistent with their known circulation patterns (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5B,C through parabiosis experiments.

claim: ~80% of splenic iNKT cells are of host origin in parabiotic pairs.
source: In contrast, ~80% of splenic iNKT cells were of host origin (Figure 5B,C), confirming that the majority of splenic iNKT cells are not circulating (Thomas et al., 2011).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5B,C through parabiosis experiments.

claim: The majority of splenic iNKT cells are not circulating.
source: In contrast, ~80% of splenic iNKT cells were of host origin (Figure 5B,C), confirming that the majority of splenic iNKT cells are not circulating (Thomas et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thomas et al., 2011 and confirmed by parabiosis data.

claim: >95% of thymic iNKT cells are of host origin in parabiotic pairs.
source: Remarkably, >95% of thymic iNKT cells were of host origin (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5B,C through parabiosis experiments.

claim: iNKT cells in the thymus are largely tissue-resident.
source: Considering that thymic iNKT effector subsets are negative for Rag2GFP (Figure 1A), these data suggest that iNKT cells in the thymus are largely tissue-resident.
evidence: Inferred from the >95% host origin of thymic iNKT cells in parabiosis and their Rag2GFP negativity.

claim: Transferred Tbx21GFP+ NKT1 cells are rarely recovered from spleen 5 days after intra-thymic transfer.
source: In contrast to thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells, wherein a substantial number of transferred cells were recovered from spleen 5 days after transfer, the transferred Tbx21GFP+ NKT1 cells were rarely recovered from spleen (Figure 5D,E), strongly suggest that CCR7+ iNKT cells efficiently emigrate thymus while iNKT effector subsets are retained in the thymus.
evidence: Shown in Figure 5D,E through intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: CCR7+ iNKT cells efficiently emigrate from the thymus while iNKT effector subsets are retained in the thymus.
source: In contrast to thymic CCR7+ iNKT cells, wherein a substantial number of transferred cells were recovered from spleen 5 days after transfer, the transferred Tbx21GFP+ NKT1 cells were rarely recovered from spleen (Figure 5D,E), strongly suggest that CCR7+ iNKT cells efficiently emigrate thymus while iNKT effector subsets are retained in the thymus.
evidence: Inferred from the differential recovery of CCR7+ vs Tbx21GFP+ cells in spleen after intra-thymic transfer.

claim: Peripheral iNKT effector subsets are not directly derived from thymic iNKT effector subsets, but rather develop from CCR7+ iNKT progenitors.
source: Together, these results show that peripheral iNKT effector subsets are not directly derived from thymic iNKT effector subsets, but rather develop from the CCR7+ iNKT progenitors, and indicate that thymic and peripheral pools of iNKT effector subsets do not exchange.
evidence: Inferred from parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: Thymic and peripheral pools of iNKT effector subsets do not exchange.
source: Together, these results show that peripheral iNKT effector subsets are not directly derived from thymic iNKT effector subsets, but rather develop from the CCR7+ iNKT progenitors, and indicate that thymic and peripheral pools of iNKT effector subsets do not exchange.
evidence: Inferred from parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: NKT1 and NKT17 cells highly express the classical tissue residency molecules CD69 and CD103, respectively.
source: Consistent with their tissue residency, NKT1 and NKT17 cells highly express the classical tissue residency molecules CD69 and CD103, respectively (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: Comparable numbers of NKT1 cells are observed in Cd69+/+, Cd69+/– and Cd69–/– mice in both thymus and spleen.
source: To evaluate whether CD69 and CD103 are required for the thymic retention of NKT1 and NKT17 cells, we analyzed Cd69+/+, Cd69+/– and Cd69–/– mice. We observed comparable number of NKT1 cells among these mice in both thymus and spleen (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C through analysis of Cd69 knockout mice.

claim: Blocking CD103 and E-Cadherin interaction does not result in loss of thymic NKT17 cells nor increase of NKT17 cells in the RTE and peripheral iNKT cell population.
source: To block CD103 interaction with E-Cadherin on epithelial cells, monoclonal antibodies (mAb) against CD103 and E-Cadherin were intra-thymically injected three times (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E). Combined with intra-thymic biotin labeling to track RTE iNKT, we did not observe loss of thymic NKT17 cells nor increase of NKT17 cells in the RTE and peripheral iNKT cells population (Figure 5—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E,F through antibody blocking experiments.

claim: The thymic retention of iNKT effector subsets is unlikely to solely rely on either CD69 or CD103.
source: These data indicate the thymic retention of iNKT effector subsets is unlikely to solely rely on either CD69 or CD103.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of effect of CD69 deficiency or CD103 blocking on thymic retention.

claim: ~50% of NKT1 (NK1.1+ CD44+) cells are Ifn-γYFP positive.
source: To ask whether NKT1 cells might have effects in the thymus, we investigated if they were producing IFN-γ in the steady state using IFN-γ reporter mice. We observed that ~50% of NKT1 (NK1.1+ CD44+) cells were Ifn-γYFP positive (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5F,G using IFN-γ reporter mice.

claim: Qa2 expression on mature thymocytes is interferon dependent.
source: Furthermore, Qa2 expression on mature thymocytes was recently shown to be interferon dependent (Xing et al., 2016), and was reduced in absence of iNKT cells (Figure 5H,I), comparable to that observed in IFN-γ receptor-deficient mice (Figure 5I), showing that the IFN-γ produced by NKT1 cells is biologically active, although the functional relevance remains unclear.
evidence: Supported by citation to Xing et al., 2016.

claim: Qa2 expression on mature thymocytes is reduced in absence of iNKT cells.
source: Furthermore, Qa2 expression on mature thymocytes was recently shown to be interferon dependent (Xing et al., 2016), and was reduced in absence of iNKT cells (Figure 5H,I), comparable to that observed in IFN-γ receptor-deficient mice (Figure 5I), showing that the IFN-γ produced by NKT1 cells is biologically active, although the functional relevance remains unclear.
evidence: Shown in Figure 5H,I through analysis of Cd1d KO mice.

claim: The IFN-γ produced by NKT1 cells is biologically active.
source: Furthermore, Qa2 expression on mature thymocytes was recently shown to be interferon dependent (Xing et al., 2016), and was reduced in absence of iNKT cells (Figure 5H,I), comparable to that observed in IFN-γ receptor-deficient mice (Figure 5I), showing that the IFN-γ produced by NKT1 cells is biologically active, although the functional relevance remains unclear.
evidence: Inferred from the reduction of Qa2 expression in Cd1d KO mice similar to IFN-γ receptor-deficient mice.

claim: iNKT cells regulate mTEC differentiation through the production of RANKL.
source: Lastly, iNKT cells have been shown to regulate mTEC differentiation through the production of RANKL (White et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to White et al., 2014.

claim: NKT2 and NKT17 cells are the exclusive producers of RANKL among iNKT cells.
source: We demonstrate here that NKT2 and NKT17 cells are the exclusive producers of RANKL among iNKT cells (Figure 5J).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5J through flow cytometry analysis.

claim: The absence of iNKT cells results in specific reduction of Aire+ medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC).
source: Consistent with a previous report (White et al., 2014), the absence of iNKT cells resulted in specific reduction of Aire+medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC), while the number of total TEC was not affected (Figure 5K,L).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5K,L through analysis of Cd1d KO mice and supported by citation to White et al., 2014.

claim: The number of total TEC is not affected by the absence of iNKT cells.
source: Consistent with a previous report (White et al., 2014), the absence of iNKT cells resulted in specific reduction of Aire+medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC), while the number of total TEC was not affected (Figure 5K,L).
evidence: Shown in Figure 5K,L through analysis of Cd1d KO mice.

claim: iNKT cells modulate thymic homeostasis.
source: Together these data strongly suggest iNKT cells modulate thymic homeostasis and indicate the possibility that they might further influence T cell development.
evidence: Inferred from the effects of iNKT cells on Qa2 expression and Aire+ mTEC numbers.

claim: Different inbred strains have strikingly different ratios of iNKT effector subsets in the thymus.
source: Given that different inbred strains have strikingly different ratios of iNKT effector subsets in the thymus, our data imply that retention of lipid specific effector T cells in the thymus fine-tunes T cell development and tissue homeostasis.
evidence: Stated as an observation in the field.

claim: Retention of lipid specific effector T cells in the thymus fine-tunes T cell development and tissue homeostasis.
source: Given that different inbred strains have strikingly different ratios of iNKT effector subsets in the thymus, our data imply that retention of lipid specific effector T cells in the thymus fine-tunes T cell development and tissue homeostasis.
evidence: Inferred from the functional effects of thymic iNKT cells and strain differences.

claim: PLZFhi iNKT cells comprise a mixture of progenitors and mature IL-4 producing NKT2 effector cells.
source: Previously, PLZFhi iNKT cells have been defined as NKT2 cells, however, our data strongly suggested that CCR7+ PLZFhi iNKT cells had multi-lineage potential in both the thymus and periphery. Thus, PLZFhi iNKT cells comprise a mixture of progenitors and mature IL-4 producing NKT2 effector cells.
evidence: Inferred from the multi-lineage potential of CCR7+ PLZFhi iNKT cells demonstrated in the study.

claim: CCR7 directs iNKT cells to localize to the thymic medulla, which plays a critical role in their differentiation to effector subsets.
source: Moreover, our data demonstrate that CCR7 not only marks the precursors but also directs iNKT cells to localize to the thymic medulla, which plays a critical role in their differentiation to effector subsets.
evidence: Demonstrated through Ccr7 deficiency experiments showing impaired medullary localization and differentiation.

claim: Ccr7 deficient mice harbor fewer thymic iNKT cells.
source: This is consistent with a previous report, which showed that Ccr7 deficient mice harbor fewer thymic iNKT cells (Cowan et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cowan et al., 2014.

claim: All three iNKT effector subsets localize predominantly to the medulla.
source: Considering the predominant medullary localization of all three iNKT effector subsets (Lee et al., 2015), it would seem that medullary factors are crucial for the differentiation and/or maintenance/survival of iNKT effector subsets.
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Medullary factors are crucial for the differentiation and/or maintenance/survival of iNKT effector subsets.
source: Considering the predominant medullary localization of all three iNKT effector subsets (Lee et al., 2015), it would seem that medullary factors are crucial for the differentiation and/or maintenance/survival of iNKT effector subsets.
evidence: Inferred from the medullary localization of effector subsets and the requirement for CCR7-mediated medullary localization for differentiation.

claim: IL-15 derived from medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC) is implicated in the generation of T-bet+ NKT1 cells.
source: Indeed, IL-15 derived from medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTEC) was implicated in the generation of T-bet+ NKT1 cells (White et al., 2014), (Cui et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to White et al., 2014 and Cui et al., 2014.

claim: MAIT cells are restricted to MR1 and recognize riboflavin metabolites.
source: Another type of innate-like T cells, MAIT cells, which are restricted to MR1 and recognize riboflavin metabolites, have gained interest recently.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: iNKT cells and MAIT cells have parallels in their development and functions.
source: A number of studies indicated a parallel between these iNKT cells and innate-like T cells in their development and functions (Koay et al., 2016; Wang and Hogquist, 2016; Rahimpour et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Koay et al., 2016; Wang and Hogquist, 2016; Rahimpour et al., 2015.

claim: Both mature iNKT and MAIT cells are poised effector cells, producing large amounts of cytokines upon stimulation.
source: For example, both mature iNKT and MAIT cells are poised effector cells, producing large amounts of cytokines upon stimulation; both express and depend on PLZF; and both are composed of effector subsets analogous to CD4 T helper subsets.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Both iNKT and MAIT cells express and depend on PLZF.
source: For example, both mature iNKT and MAIT cells are poised effector cells, producing large amounts of cytokines upon stimulation; both express and depend on PLZF; and both are composed of effector subsets analogous to CD4 T helper subsets.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Both iNKT and MAIT cells are composed of effector subsets analogous to CD4 T helper subsets.
source: For example, both mature iNKT and MAIT cells are poised effector cells, producing large amounts of cytokines upon stimulation; both express and depend on PLZF; and both are composed of effector subsets analogous to CD4 T helper subsets.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: CCR7 marks a population of immature MAIT cells after agonist selection.
source: We show here that, similar to iNKT cells, CCR7 also marks a population of immature MAIT cells after the agonist selection.
evidence: Demonstrated through analysis of CCR7+ MAIT cells in Rag2GFP mice.

claim: Mature iNKT effector subsets, including NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17, exist in both the thymus and peripheral tissues.
source: Mature iNKT effector subsets, including NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17, exist in both the thymus and peripheral tissues (Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lee et al., 2015.

claim: A thymic NK1.1− iNKT cell emigrates.
source: Previous work showed that a thymic NK1.1− iNKT cell emigrates (Benlagha et al., 2002; Pellicci et al., 2002), but the work was performed before it was appreciated that mature NKT2 and NKT17 effector cells are also NK1.1−.
evidence: Supported by citations to Benlagha et al., 2002 and Pellicci et al., 2002.

claim: Mature NKT2 and NKT17 effector cells are NK1.1−.
source: Previous work showed that a thymic NK1.1− iNKT cell emigrates (Benlagha et al., 2002; Pellicci et al., 2002), but the work was performed before it was appreciated that mature NKT2 and NKT17 effector cells are also NK1.1−.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: All thymic iNKT effector cells are long-term residents that do not emigrate.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that all thymic iNKT effector cells are long-term residents that do not emigrate, and that peripheral iNKT effector subsets derive from CCR7+ iNKT cells that emigrate from the thymus.
evidence: Demonstrated through parabiosis and intra-thymic transfer experiments.

claim: Peripheral iNKT effector subsets derive from CCR7+ iNKT cells that emigrate from the thymus.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that all thymic iNKT effector cells are long-term residents that do not emigrate, and that peripheral iNKT effector subsets derive from CCR7+ iNKT cells that emigrate from the thymus.
evidence: Demonstrated through intra-thymic labeling and transfer experiments.

claim: iNKT cells can participate in immunity to infection.
source: iNKT cells can participate in immunity to infection (Bendelac et al., 2007), but they can also regulate tissue homeostasis in the steady state (Lynch et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2015; Lynch et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bendelac et al., 2007.

claim: iNKT cells can regulate tissue homeostasis in the steady state.
source: iNKT cells can participate in immunity to infection (Bendelac et al., 2007), but they can also regulate tissue homeostasis in the steady state (Lynch et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2015; Lynch et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lynch et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2015; Lynch et al., 2016; Lee et al., 2016.

claim: NKT2 cells constitutively produce IL-4 which drives Eomesodermin (Eomes) expression and a memory-like functional state in CD8 T cells.
source: An effect of NKT2 cells on CD8 T cell development in the steady state is well supported by previous data showing their constitutive production of IL-4 drives Eomesodermin (Eomes) expression and a memory-like functional state in CD8 T cells (Lee et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2013 and Lee et al., 2015.

claim: Thymic resident NKT1 cells produce IFN-γ and promote Qa2 expression in CD4 and CD8 SP thymocytes.
source: In this report, we further show that thymic resident NKT1 cells produce IFN-γ and promote Qa2 expression in CD4 and CD8 SP thymocytes.
evidence: Demonstrated through analysis of IFN-γ production and Qa2 expression in Cd1d KO mice.

claim: T cells up-regulate Qa2 expression during their maturation in the thymus.
source: T cells up-regulate Qa2 expression during their maturation in the thymus, and type I interferon signaling has been implicated in this process (Xing et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xing et al., 2016.

claim: Type I interferon signaling has been implicated in Qa2 up-regulation during T cell maturation in the thymus.
source: T cells up-regulate Qa2 expression during their maturation in the thymus, and type I interferon signaling has been implicated in this process (Xing et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Xing et al., 2016.

claim: IFN-γ might function synergistically with type I interferon to influence Qa2 expression.
source: It is possible that IFN-γ might function synergistically with type I interferon to influence Qa2 expression.
evidence: Speculated based on the effects of IFN-γ and type I interferon on Qa2 expression.

claim: Both NKT2 and NKT17 cells express RANK ligand.
source: Lastly, we show both NKT2 and NKT17 cells express RANK ligand, and together could promote Aire expression in mTEC in supporting central tolerance.
evidence: Shown through flow cytometry analysis of RANKL expression.

claim: NKT2 and NKT17 cells together could promote Aire expression in mTEC in supporting central tolerance.
source: Lastly, we show both NKT2 and NKT17 cells express RANK ligand, and together could promote Aire expression in mTEC in supporting central tolerance.
evidence: Inferred from RANKL expression and the reduction of Aire+ mTEC in Cd1d KO mice.

claim: A small number of CCR7+ iNKT cells express lower amounts of PLZF, LEF1 or CD4.
source: It is worth mentioning that a small number of CCR7+ iNKT cells express lower amounts of PLZF, LEF1 or CD4.
evidence: Observed in flow cytometry data.

claim: The development of iNKT cells in the thymus is a dynamic process.
source: Indeed, the development of iNKT cells in the thymus is a dynamic process, even though the CCR7+ iNKT cell population is largely immature and maintains precursor potential, it seems likely some of these cells have begun to receive development signals and to differentiate, prior to having completely lost CCR7 expression.
evidence: Inferred from the heterogeneity observed within CCR7+ iNKT cells.

claim: CCR7 is critical for optimal differentiation of all three iNKT subsets.
source: Of interest, though CCR7 is critical for optimal differentiation of all three iNKT subsets, NKT17 cells seem to be most affected by CCR7 deficiency.
evidence: Observed in mixed bone marrow chimera experiments with Ccr7 KO cells.

claim: NKT17 cells seem to be most affected by CCR7 deficiency.
source: Of interest, though CCR7 is critical for optimal differentiation of all three iNKT subsets, NKT17 cells seem to be most affected by CCR7 deficiency.
evidence: Observed in mixed bone marrow chimera experiments with Ccr7 KO cells.

claim: The differentiation or maintenance of NKT17 cells may be more dependent on as yet undefined factors in the medullary environment.
source: Since NKT1, NKT2 and NKT17 are all localized to the thymic medulla, it is unclear what might cause this effect. Possibly, the differentiation or maintenance of NKT17 cells is more dependent on as yet undefined factors in the medullary environment.
evidence: Speculated based on the differential effect of CCR7 deficiency on NKT17 cells.

claim: CCR7+PLZFhi iNKT cells represent a pool of precursor cells for all three iNKT effector subsets in thymus and periphery.
source: In summary, we demonstrate here that the sub-population of CCR7+PLZFhi iNKT cells represent a pool of precursor cells for all three iNKT effector subsets in thymus and periphery.
evidence: Main conclusion summarizing the findings of the study.

claim: The thymic and peripheral iNKT effector subsets are resident and do not exchange.
source: The thymic and peripheral iNKT effector subsets are resident and do not exchange, therefore depend on CCR7+ iNKT progenitors for their establishment.
evidence: Main conclusion summarizing the findings of the study.

claim: Thymic and peripheral iNKT effector subsets depend on CCR7+ iNKT progenitors for their establishment.
source: The thymic and peripheral iNKT effector subsets are resident and do not exchange, therefore depend on CCR7+ iNKT progenitors for their establishment.
evidence: Main conclusion summarizing the findings of the study.
